institutionName: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose NTNU because the courses sounded really interesting and relevant to what I study. I was also excited about the chance to experience Norwegian culture and everyday life. Plus, the nature in and around Trondheim really appealed to me. It's such a beautiful place to live and study.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find the information I needed upon arrival. NTNU provided clear guidance.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn’t receive any specific assistance upon arrival, but the information provided beforehand was clear enough that I managed everything on my own without any issues.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was very easy to find off-campus housing. I used
hybel.no
, which had lots of good options and made the process straightforward. I’d definitely recommend it to other students looking for a place to stay.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus worked really well for me, especially since I was living with my partner, who was working remotely. But if you're very social or want to meet a lot of new people, it might be a better fit to live in a dorm room or share an apartment with other students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They have a dedicated website where you register and choose your courses. Everything was straightforward and well explained, so I didn’t have any problems.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I didn’t need any help during the process, so I’m not entirely sure what kind of support was available. But everything was clear and easy to manage on my own.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was quite successful in registering for the classes I wanted. There was one course that wasn’t available, because they didn't have it anymore, but otherwise I got into all the courses I was interested in.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn’t run into any problems with registration, so I don’t have specific advice. But I’d recommend reading the instructions carefully and registering as early as possible to make sure you get the courses you want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took three bachelor’s level courses and one master’s level course. I found the bachelor’s courses a bit too easy, but they were still interesting. The master’s course, on the other hand, was more challenging and engaging. I really enjoyed it and felt like I learned a lot from it.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It's the same.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
They have a student sports association, NTNUI, which has over 60 different sports and activities. They also have cabins in nature that students can use for weekend trips, which is a great way to explore the area. And you can borrow gear for hiking, cross-country skiing, fishing, and more from Bumerang for free. 

There are also many student organizations and events throughout the year. NTNU hosts big cultural festivals like UKA and ISFiT, and there are plenty of student groups related to music, dance, theatre, and other interests. The Student Society is very active.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend hiking in the summer and cross-country skiing in the winter. The nature around Trondheim is absolutely beautiful and very different from what I'm used to in Denmark. It’s a great way to experience the Norwegian landscape

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to adjust to the local culture. The cultural differences were small, so I felt comfortable pretty quickly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I found it pretty easy to socialize through the courses. Group work and class discussions were a good way to get to know both local and other exchange students. Just being open and willing to talk during breaks or after class really helped. Joining student activities or events can also be a great way to meet people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated everything about the culture. The strong connection to nature, the balance between work and free time, and the friendliness of the people in Trondheim all made a great impression on me. I also enjoyed that Trondheim is a very historical city. It gave me the chance to learn more about Norwegian history, which I found really interesting.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Get out into nature as much as you can. It’s incredibly easy and accessible in Trondheim. Whether it’s hiking, skiing, or just going for a walk. 

Explore the city. Trondheim has a lot to offer with its cozy cafés, interesting museums, and historical sites. Take time to enjoy what the city itself has to offer, not just the university.

Pe prepared for the weather. Make sure to have good waterproof shoes.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: One thing that might be useful to know is that things are very well-organized at NTNU, so don’t stress too much. Most practical information is easy to find, and people are helpful if you need anything.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was getting to live in a completely new environment. I loved the nature, and it was great to meet both local and international students. It gave me new perspectives, both academically and personally, and I really grew from the experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during my exchange was working in a group that didn’t function well. It was a bit difficult to manage expectations and communication, especially in a new academic setting. However, the teacher was very helpful and supportive, which made a big difference and helped me get through the situation.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
